name: Citations and Grounded Answers
question: Can every sentence in the answer be traced to a source?
summary: Makes answers checkable. The model answers only from the retrieved passages and cites a source for each claim; the system checks that the cited text really is in that source and supports the sentence, drops what is unsupported, and says “not found” when nothing supports an answer. Sources are shown with the document, section, page and effective date, and superseded versions are filtered out before the model sees them.
useCases: Policy, HR, legal and compliance assistants
Customer-facing answers about fees, limits and eligibility
Any answer a person will act on or an auditor may question

items.detail: each passage labelled with title, section and date
a source after every sentence, not one list at the end
the exact span the claim rests on
the span exists in the source and supports the claim

steps: Label each passage with its title, section and effective date, and filter out superseded versions
Instruct the model to answer only from the sources and cite each sentence
Verify every citation in code and drop sentences that fail
Say “not found” when nothing is supported, and show the sources
pitfalls: Citations that point to a real passage that does not say what the sentence claims
Valid citations to an outdated version of a policy
Forcing an answer when the sources are empty
caption: Illustrative: Kaveri Bank, a fictional bank, runs a staff policy assistant with 100 test questions.

code.text: current = [p for p in passages if p.is_current]        # drop superseded
system="Answer only from the documents. If they do not answer, say so.",
ok = [c for c in cites if c.cited_text in current[c.document_index].text]
sources += [(c.document_title, c.cited_text) for c in ok]
reply = "".join(answer) if sources else "I could not find this in the policies."

steps.title: Label the sources, current versions only
steps.text: Each passage becomes a document with its title, section and effective date. The 2023 leave policy is superseded, so it is filtered out before the model sees it.

steps.title: Switch on citations and ground the prompt
steps.text: With citations enabled, the model’s answer comes back as text blocks, each carrying the source spans it relied on. The system prompt says: answer only from the documents.

steps.title: Read what each sentence rests on
steps.text: Every citation names the document and quotes the exact cited text, for example “10 working days of paternity leave”.

steps.title: Verify in code, drop what fails
steps.text: Check that each cited span is really in that document. A sentence that states a fact without a valid citation is dropped, not shown.

steps.title: No support, no answer
steps.text: If nothing survives verification, the assistant says it could not find the answer. Declining beats a confident guess about someone’s leave.

steps.title: Show the sources
steps.text: The reply ends with each source’s title, section and effective date, so staff can check it in seconds.

pros: Every claim can be checked in seconds
Verification drops unsupported sentences before anyone reads them
Abstaining beats a confident wrong answer
Auditors and staff can see which version of a policy was used
cons: Stricter grounding means more “not found” replies
Verification code and version metadata to maintain
Valid citations can still point to the wrong version unless filtered
avoidWhen: Creative or brainstorming tasks where there is no source to cite
Internal drafts that a person rewrites anyway (cite loosely, verify later)

practice.scenario: Kaveri Bank, a fictional bank, runs a policy assistant for its staff. Only current policy versions are retrieved; each is passed as a document with its title, section and effective date and with citations enabled. Every sentence in the answer must carry a citation whose text is found in its source, or it is dropped. With nothing left, the assistant says it could not find the answer.

industries.use: Staff policy assistants for leave, conduct and product rules
Answers from clinical guidelines with the exact passage shown
Research answers that cite the clause and the version

practice.analogy: A good analyst's report: every number has a footnote, and a reviewer can check any footnote in seconds.

library.name: Anthropic Citations
library.what: Pass sources as document blocks with citations enabled; the answer comes back as text blocks with the exact cited spans.

practice.note: Check the current model names and the citation fields in the API documentation for your SDK version.

samples.code:
import anthropic

client = anthropic.Anthropic()
policy = "Paternity leave: employees get 10 working days, to be taken within 3 months of the birth."

msg = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-sonnet-5", max_tokens=500,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": [
        {"type": "document", "title": "Leave policy §5 · effective 1 Apr 2026",
         "source": {"type": "text", "media_type": "text/plain", "data": policy},
         "citations": {"enabled": True}},
        {"type": "text", "text": "How many days of paternity leave do I get?"}]}])

for block in msg.content:
    if block.type == "text":
        print(block.text)
        for c in block.citations or []:
            assert c.cited_text in policy          # verify against the source
            print("   cited:", c.cited_text)

numericDrill.question: An assistant answers 80 questions; 9% contain an unsupported claim. Claim-level citations cut that by a fifth, and verification removes 80% of what remains. About how many answers still contain an unsupported claim?

interview.question: How do you stop a RAG assistant from making things up?
interview.answer: Ground it: answer only from retrieved sources, cite each sentence, verify each citation against its source in code, drop unsupported sentences and abstain when nothing is supported. Measure faithfulness on an eval set and track the abstain rate.

interview.question: Your citations are all valid but some answers are outdated. Why?
interview.answer: Superseded documents are still in the index, so the model cites real text from old versions. Store version and effective-date metadata, filter to current versions before retrieval and show dates with sources.

mistakes.fix: Verify that the cited text is in the source and supports the claim

mistakes.mistake: Leaving old versions in the index
mistakes.fix: Filter by version metadata before retrieval

quiz.question: What does “grounded” mean for a RAG answer?
options: Every claim is supported by the provided sources
quiz.explanation: Groundedness is support by sources, not style.

quiz.question: A citation points to a real policy passage, but the passage does not say what the sentence claims. What catches this?
options: Checking that the cited span supports the claim, for figures that the number appears in it
quiz.explanation: Existence of a citation is not support; verify the content.

quiz.question: All citations verify, yet answers quote a 2023 policy replaced in 2025. What is missing?
options: Version filtering by effective date or a current flag
quiz.explanation: Valid citations to outdated sources pass verification; filter versions before retrieval.

quiz.question: Which belong in a grounded-answer pipeline? Select all that apply.
options: Let the model add facts it is confident about
quiz.explanation: Model knowledge without a source breaks grounding.

quiz.question: Nothing in the sources answers the question. What should the assistant do?
options: Say it could not find the answer in the documents
Pick the closest passage and answer
quiz.explanation: Abstaining beats a confident wrong answer.

quiz.question: Staff take 90 seconds to check an answer without citations and 15 seconds with a source per sentence. For 400 answers a day, how many staff-hours are saved?
Why cite after each sentence rather than listing sources at the end?
options: Each claim can be traced and checked on its own
quiz.explanation: Claim-level citations make checking fast and specific.

quiz.question: With Anthropic’s Citations feature, what comes back with the answer?
options: Only a list of document titles
Text blocks carrying the exact cited text and the document it came from
quiz.explanation: The cited spans are what you verify.

quiz.question: Which metadata should each source carry for display? Select all that apply.
quiz.explanation: People need to find and trust the source; vectors mean nothing to them.

quiz.question: Verification removes 80% of unsupported claims. If 6 answers of 80 have one before verification, how many remain?
Adding an abstain rule costs 3 answerable questions but declines 7 more unanswerable ones. Is it worth it?
options: Usually, where wrong answers are costly; measure both numbers
It depends on the model size
quiz.explanation: Weigh false abstentions against confident wrong answers for your use.

quiz.question: What does the Ragas faithfulness metric measure?
options: How many claims in the answer are supported by the retrieved context
quiz.explanation: It checks claims against context.

quiz.question: Where should superseded versions be filtered?
options: Before retrieval, as a metadata filter
In the prompt, by asking the model to ignore them
quiz.explanation: Filter before the model sees them; prompts are not a reliable filter.

quiz.question: A citizen assistant must show where each rule comes from. What is the minimum?
options: A link to the ministry home page
The document, section and date for each cited claim
quiz.explanation: Specific, checkable sources.

quiz.question: Which are warning signs of weak grounding? Select all that apply.
options: Citations whose text is not in the source
Numbers in the answer that do not appear in the cited span
quiz.explanation: Length is not a grounding signal.

quiz.question: The model cites passage 3 for “the fee is ₹500”, but passage 3 says ₹250. What should verification do?
options: Reject the sentence because the figure is not in the cited text
quiz.explanation: For figures, check the number itself appears in the cited span.

quiz.question: A free prompt yields 18% answers with unsupported claims; a grounded prompt yields 9%. What does grounding alone not guarantee?
options: That the remaining claims are supported; verification is still needed
quiz.explanation: Prompts reduce the rate; code checks enforce it.

quiz.question: Why is “not found” sometimes the best answer?
options: When sources do not support an answer, any answer would be a guess
quiz.explanation: Declining preserves trust.

quiz.question: Where should citation verification run?
options: In code, after generation and before display
quiz.explanation: Deterministic checks after generation, before anyone sees the answer.

quiz.question: What does citation verification not catch?
options: A cited span missing from the source
A correct citation to an outdated document
A number that differs from the cited text
quiz.explanation: The span is real; the document is stale. Use version filtering.
